entry.literal: Merodach Baladan son of Baladan; documents and a gift; and he heard … and he recovered; and he rejoiced over them; the house of his treasure; the good oil; all the house of his vessels; these men; house; your fathers; (to) Babylon; and of your sons; they will take; and he said: for / indeed / if only there will be peace and truth in my days
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: 'Merodach-baladan the son of Baladan', 'letters and a present', 'for he heard that he had been sick, and was recovered', 'was glad of them', 'the house of his precious things', 'the precious oil', 'all the house of his armor', 'these men', 'thy house', 'thy fathers', 'of thy sons … shall they take away', 'He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days'. JPS 1917: 'a letter and a present', 'his treasure-house', 'If but there shall be peace and truth in my days'. NJPS: '[envoys with] a letter and a gift', 'was pleased by their coming', 'his treasure house', 'the fragrant oil', 'all his armory', 'palace', 'your ancestors', 'will be taken', 'For he thought, "It means that safety is assured for my time"' (note 'Lit. "there shall be safety and faithfulness in"'). 2 Kgs 20:12-19 (ASV): 'Berodach-baladan', 'hearkened unto them', 'Is it not so, if peace and truth shall be in my days?'. (ASV and KJV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917, NJPS (Tanakh: The Holy Scriptures, published by JPS, 1985; not the Gender-Sensitive Edition), Fox (The Early Prophets, 2014) and the Metsudah Tanach (Kings) via Sefaria API v3; MT of Isa 39, 37:14 and 2 Kgs 20:12-19 (Westminster Leningrad Codex via Sefaria); all checked 2026-11-27.) Not verified: LXX, 1QIsaᵃ, NRSV, BDB/HALOT, the Akkadian bīt nakkamti etymology of nᵉḵōṯ.
entry.wohChoice: 39:1 'Merodach-baladan son of Baladan' (MT Isaiah and ASV spelling; the English pattern '-baladan son of Baladan' is fixed for the shared text; at 2 Kgs 20:12 the MT reads bᵉrōʾḏaḵ, 'Berodach-baladan' in ASV, and whether Kings keeps its own form is escalated); sᵉp̄ārîm 'letters' (plural kept; sēp̄er = 'letter' for a diplomatic letter, outside `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29`; orchestrator ruling, wave I-6: one noun, 'letter', with the number following each verse's grammar, so 37:14 'the letter' with its singular suffixes and 39:1 'letters'); minḥāh 'a present' (central minchah-tribute-gift-of-appeasement); wayyišmaʿ … wayyeḥĕzāq 'for he heard that he had been sick and had recovered'. 39:2 wayyiśmaḥ ʿălêhem 'was glad of them' (MT Isaiah; Kings wayyišmaʿ in commentary); bêṯ nᵉḵōṯô (qere) 'the house of his precious things' (ASV); haššemen haṭṭôḇ 'the fine oil' (so that 'precious' renders only nᵉḵōṯ); kol-bêṯ kēlāyw 'all the house of his armor' (ASV). 39:3 hāʾănāšîm hāʾēlleh 'these men' (specific male envoys; wave I-4 rule 13). 39:2, 4, 6 bayiṯ 'house' throughout (NJPS 'palace' in commentary). 39:6 ʾăḇōṯeyḵā 'your fathers' (male royal line); bāḇel 'to Babylon'. 39:7 mibbāneyḵā 'some of your sons'; yiqqāḥû 'they shall take away' (pausal Qal imperfect 3mp, impersonal; 2 Kgs 20:18 ketiv yqḥ, qere yiqqāḥû). 39:8 'And he said: “For there shall be peace and truth in my days.”' (ASV construal; inner-speech, wish and question readings in commentary); ʾĕmeṯ 'truth' as elsewhere in the book; šālôm 'peace'.
entry.rationale: Isaiah 39 is prose shared with 2 Kgs 20:12-19, and under wave I-6 rule 3 the Isaiah line is translated on its own Masoretic text, with every difference from Kings recorded in commentary (Kings bᵉrōʾḏaḵ, kî šāmaʿ without wayyeḥĕzāq, wayyišmaʿ, nᵉḵōṯōh written without a qere, šemen without the article, the placement of kol, the absence of ʾēlay and ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ, bāḇelāh, the ketiv/qere yqḥ / yiqqāḥû, and the question hălôʾ ʾim at 20:19; MT checked). Every rendering in the entry is the wording of ASV or of JPS 1917 in modern English, except two. The partitive mibbāneyḵā 'some of your sons' (39:7) is the wording of NJPS, Fox and Metsudah (ASV and JPS 1917 'of thy sons'; checked). And haššemen haṭṭôḇ is 'the fine oil' rather than ASV's 'the precious oil', because ASV uses 'precious' in the same verse for nᵉḵōṯ, and two different Hebrew words should not share one English adjective; 'fine oil' is the rendering of Fox and of the Metsudah translation at 2 Kgs 20:13 (checked). The ASV 'the house of his precious things' is kept for bêṯ nᵉḵōṯô, against 'treasure house' (JPS 1917, NJPS), because it keeps bêṯ as 'house' beside bêṯ kēlāyw in the same verse and keeps 'treasures' for the different noun ʾôṣārôṯ; the Akkadian loan-etymology of nᵉḵōṯ (Fox: 'a loan word from Akkadian', checked) is given in commentary. Male nouns stay male where they denote specific men: the envoys (39:3), the king's royal predecessors (39:6) and the sons who will become sārîsîm (39:7), in line with wave I-4 rule 13; NJPS 'your ancestors' is recorded. At 39:8 the clause wayyōʾmer kî yihyeh šālôm weʾĕmeṯ bᵉyāmāy has three disputed points (inner speech or a second remark; causal, recitative or optative kî; the meaning of ʾĕmeṯ beside šālôm), and the versions divide (ASV/KJV 'For', JPS 1917 'If but', NJPS 'For he thought, “It means that safety is assured for my time”'); the line keeps the ASV construal because it keeps the order and the words of the Hebrew, and the commentary sets out the alternatives and the Kings question form. ʾĕmeṯ stays 'truth', the book's rendering at 10:20, 16:5, 42:3 and 48:1, and šālôm stays 'peace'; the central chesed-v-emet entry (scoped to ḥeseḏ weʾĕmeṯ) and the overlay ra-calamity-shalom-well-being-isaiah-45-7 (scoped to 45:7) are not applied. The entry is direct: every choice is a standard rendering attested in the checked versions, and no reading of the project is carried in the line. Orchestrator ruling (wave I-6, after review): the sᵉp̄ārîm of 37:14 and 39:1 share one English noun, 'letter', and the number follows each verse's grammar. At 37:14 the singular suffixes of wayyiqrāʾēhû and wayyip̄rᵉśēhû give 'the letter'; at 39:1, where nothing in the verse marks the number, the plural is kept, 'letters'.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-6 (Isa 39): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 39 — The envoys of Merodach-baladan and the word of exile to Babylon' is ratified (the envoys are the hāʾănāšîm of 39:3; the name follows the Isaiah MT, see lexical-cruxes-isaiah-39). Quotation marks: the speeches of 39:3-4 and 39:8 are quoted; Isaiah's oracle runs as one quotation from 'Hear the word of YHWH of hosts' (39:5) to the end of 39:7, with 'says YHWH' (39:6) inside it. JPS 1917 marks the same span; ASV prints no marks (checked 2026-11-27).

Wave I-6 (Isa 39): 'the word of YHWH of hosts' at 39:5 (ASV 'Jehovah of hosts'; JPS 1917 'the LORD of hosts'; NJPS 'the LORD of Hosts'; checked 2026-11-27). The parallel 2 Kgs 20:16 has dᵉḇar-YHWH without ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ (MT checked); the difference is recorded in commentary.

Wave I-6 (Isa 39): at 39:2 the ketiv נכתה / qere נְכֹתוֹ (bêṯ nᵉḵōṯô 'the house of his precious things') is an orthographic pair, the older -h spelling of the third-person suffix against the usual -ô; the qere is followed and the sense is unchanged. The parallel 2 Kgs 20:13 writes נְכֹתֹה in the text without a qere, and at 2 Kgs 20:18 the ketiv יקח / qere יִקָּחוּ stands where Isa 39:7 has yiqqāḥû in the text (MT via Sefaria, checked 2026-11-27); both Kings facts are recorded in commentary at Isa 39:2 and 39:7.

changes.wohChoice: 'the temple' - the standard rendering, with the palace / royal-audience-hall register of hêḵāl noted in commentary rather than surfaced in the line. Context clause (wave I-6): where hêḵāl is the residence of a human king it is 'palace' (39:7 bᵉhêḵal meleḵ bāḇel 'in the palace of the king of Babylon'), as the central ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus provides.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-6 context clause (Isa 39:7): hêḵāl means both palace and temple (the rationale above), and the choice between them is made by context. At 39:7 the sons of Hezekiah will serve bᵉhêḵal meleḵ bāḇel, the residence of a human king, so the line has 'in the palace of the king of Babylon' with ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (checked 2026-11-27) and under the context clause of the central ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus ('temple' or 'palace' by context). 'The temple' stays the rendering wherever hêḵāl is the house of YHWH (6:1; 44:28). The clause is recorded here so that this entry does not appear to require 'temple' at a royal site.
